'''Michael George Bulmer''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 10 May 1931)<ref name=bio/><ref name="MCreg">{{cite book|editor1-last=Levens|editor1-first=R.G.C.|title=Merton College Register 1900–1964|date=1964|publisher=Basil Blackwell|location=Oxford|page=400}}</ref> is a British biostatistician. He is an emeritus fellow of [[Wolfson College, Oxford]], and a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of London]].<ref name=bio/> He is known for his work in [[quantitative genetics]] and on the [[biology]] of [[twin]]ning,<ref name=rs/> as well as for his 2003 biography of [[Francis Galton]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Smocovitis |first1=Vassiliki Betty |title=Michael Bulmer xvii + 357 pp., illus., bibl., index. Baltimore/London: Johns Hopkins University Press, 2003. |journal=Isis |date=June 2007 |volume=98 |issue=2 |pages=398–399 |doi=10.1086/521468}}</ref>

==Biography==
Bulmer was born in [[Birmingham]], [[England]], in 1931. After graduating from [[Rugby School]], he studied at [[Merton College, Oxford]], from 1949 to 1957, taking a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in animal physiology in 1952, a diploma in applied statistics the following year, a [[D.Phil.]] in statistics in 1957, and a [[D.Sc.]]<ref name="MCreg" /> He then lectured at the [[University of Manchester]] from 1957 to 1959, after which he became a lecturer in [[biomathematics]] at the University of Oxford. In 1991, he left Oxford to become a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at [[Rutgers University]], where he remained until 1995.<ref name=bio>{{Cite web |url=http://michaelbulmer.com/Bulmer.html |title=Michael Bulmer Biography |website=michaelbulmer.com |access-date=2018-12-27 |archive-date=29 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180829032731/http://michaelbulmer.com/Bulmer.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
